title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: on the previous page Grothendieck reduces an injectivity statement about function fields to a geometric one. The statement is that a k-embedding of function fields K -> K' is determined by the induced outer homomorphism of geometric Galois groups pi_{K'} -> pi_K. He writes K = lim A_i and K' = lim A'_j, uses surjectivity of the transition maps between the pi_1 of regular models, and is left needing a 'more general result' about morphisms of varieties. This page states that result as Corollary 1.

Corollary 1. Let X, Y be reduced schemes of finite type over an algebraically closed field k (implicitly X connected), and let f, g : X -> Y be two morphisms such that pi_1(f) = pi_1(g) : pi_1(X) => pi_1(Y) as outer homomorphisms (for suitable base points).

(a) Suppose Y embeds, via i : Y -> G, into a commutative algebraic group G which is an extension of an abelian variety by a torus (a semi-abelian variety). Then there is a unique a with i∘g = tau_a ∘ i∘f, where tau_a is translation by a. In fact it suffices to assume H_1(f, Z_l) = H_1(g, Z_l) for a single prime l different from the characteristic.

(b) Suppose Y is an 'elementary variety', i.e. a tower of successive fibrations in (hyperbolic) curves, an Artin good neighbourhood. Suppose also that X is irreducible (and normal) and that f or g is dominant. Then f = g.

Proof of (a), begun here and finished on the next page:
- Replace Y by G. Uniqueness of a is clear.
- For existence, choose an origin o in X(k) and translate so that f(o) = g(o) = 0. One must then show f = g, using only the l-adic part of the abelianised pi_1.
- Next page: pointed maps (X, o) -> (G, 0) factor uniquely as X -> J -> G. Here J is the generalised (semi-abelian) Albanese of X and phi : J -> G is a homomorphism.
- A homomorphism of semi-abelian varieties is determined by its action on T_l, since l-power torsion is dense.
- H_1(X, Z_l) ≅ H_1(J, Z_l), hence H_1(f) = H_1(g) gives phi = psi.
- He also remarks that one cannot conclude f = g in (a): translations act trivially on pi_1(G), 'at least in char 0 or if G is an abelian variety'.

The left margin note seems to reduce (b) to X irreducible and normal (via a W ... fibrations, dominance). So (b) is the geometric anabelian-rigidity input for the field-theoretic injectivity.
errors: 'il existe un a ∈ Y (unique)': a should be a point of G(k) (namely g(o) - f(o)), not of Y, since Y is only a subvariety of G.
Connectedness of X is needed in (a), since a translation constant is only defined per connected component; the hypothesis is not stated.

The claim (next page) H_1(X, Z_l) ≅ H_1(J, Z_l) is too strong for arbitrary reduced X. For a projective nodal cubic, pi_1^ab is Z_l while the semi-abelian Albanese is trivial. What the proof needs, and what holds, is that H_1(X, Z_l) -> T_l(J) has dense (indeed full) image; for smooth X it is an isomorphism mod torsion. With that correction the argument is fine.

(b) as stated needs the elementary variety to be built from hyperbolic curves (or at least not containing G_m / elliptic factors), otherwise translations give counterexamples. This is presumably implicit in 'variété élémentaire'.

ideas.what: Morphisms into a semi-abelian variety are determined up to translation by their effect on H_1(-, Z_l), via the universal property of the generalized Albanese and density of l-power torsion
ideas.modern_name: Rigidity of maps to semi-abelian varieties / universal property of the Serre generalized Albanese; Tate-module faithfulness
ideas.where_published: Standard; possibly alluded to in La Longue Marche (1981)

ideas.what: Over an algebraically closed field, a dominant morphism into an elementary (successive hyperbolic-curve fibration) variety is determined by its outer action on geometric pi_1
ideas.modern_name: Hom-injectivity / geometric anabelian rigidity for elementary anabelian varieties (Artin neighbourhoods)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Longue Marche, letter to Faltings 1983) as conjectural framework; later Mochizuki, Tamagawa, Stix on injectivity results; complex-analytic analogue via harmonic maps (Eells–Sampson, Hartman)
ideas.where_published: La Longue Marche à travers la théorie de Galois (1981) discusses elementary anabelian varieties and rigidity

ideas.what: Reduction of injectivity of Hom(K,K') -> Hom_out(pi_{K'}, pi_K) for function fields to the geometric statement for elementary varieties
ideas.modern_name: Birational anabelian injectivity via limits of geometric fundamental groups
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (programme); Pop for the birational anabelian theorem over finitely generated fields

ideas.what: Observation that translations act trivially on pi_1(G) only in char 0 or for abelian varieties (hinting at wild Artin–Schreier phenomena for tori in char p)
ideas.modern_name: Non-triviality of translation action on the wild fundamental group of G_m in characteristic p

missed.claim: The page shows Grothendieck isolating an explicit 'abelian/semi-abelian' rigidity case (a) as the base of an induction for elementary anabelian varieties (b), with the explicit weakening to l-adic H_1 for one l. This is a concrete proof strategy rather than just a conjecture, but such injectivity statements are now known.
missed.quote: En fait, dans a), il suffit de supposer que H_1(f,Z_ℓ) = H_1(g,Z_ℓ) pour un ℓ premier à car.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical: documents that Grothendieck had a worked proof sketch of geometric Hom-injectivity (in arbitrary characteristic, using only prime-to-p data) in the Longue Marche period.

deep.surprise_reason: Part (a) is a standard Albanese/Tate-module argument. Part (b) is the expected geometric rigidity underlying anabelian injectivity, consistent with the published Longue Marche programme and later work. The page has historical interest but no result absent from the literature.
